key_big: Resolve, then use suvat in each direction.
body_html:
How to think about it

Resolve a force F at angle θ into F cos θ and F sin θ. For constant acceleration use the suvat equations; for projectiles treat horizontal (constant speed) and vertical (acceleration g) motion separately. Momentum is conserved in collisions.

Stress = F/A, strain = ΔL/L, and the Young modulus E = stress/strain. Use the area of the cross-section π(d/2)².

Example

Ball thrown horizontally at 5 m/s from 1.8 m. Range?

t = √(2 × 1.8/9.81) = 0.606 s

x = 5 × 0.606

Answer: 3.03 m

Example

Wire 2.0 m, d = 0.5 mm, 50 N, ΔL = 2.5 mm. Young modulus?

A = 1.96 × 10−7 m²

E = (50 × 2.0)/(1.96 × 10−7 × 2.5 × 10−3)

Answer: 2.0 × 1011 Pa

Common mistakes

  • Using the diameter instead of the radius for the area.
  • Letting horizontal speed change in projectile motion.
  • Forgetting that strain has no unit.

faq.q: How do you solve a projectile problem?
faq.a: Split the motion: horizontally the speed is constant; vertically the acceleration is g. Time links the two.
Tensile stress ÷ tensile strain. It measures the stiffness of a material, in pascals.
